newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rebounds strongly, cold weather helps.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rebounds strongly, cold weather helps.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures rebounded strongly on Thursday, almost totally erasing Wednesday's large losses, on the back of cold weather forecasts for the U.S. and Europe, brokers said.
The rebound was dented in the middle of the day by reports of some progress in the Iraqi oil sales deal with the United Nations, but this was shrugged off by the market, they added.
January Brent closed 59 cents up at $23.13 per barrel, having shed almost a dollar on Wednesday.
"The cold weather forecasts are very constructive and natural gas is going through the ceiling," a broker said.
"Today's performance was damn impressive. It makes me think that yesterday was just a mistake."

A cold arctic high pressure was expected to push temperatures 16-24 degrees below normal in the northern United States over the next few days, staying below normal for another week, according to private forecaster Weather Services Corp.
They also said energy usage in northwest Europe would be above normal until the middle of next week.

The restraining factor on prices was news from the United Nations in New York, brokers said, where a Western diplomat said on Wednesday that if current U.N.-sponsored inspector visits to Iraq went well, the oil sales deal could be implemented in February 1997.

Gas oil prices dropped sharply on Thursday to reflect crude's earlier drop. Dec gas oil closed $4.75 lower at $219.00 per tonne, and the Nov/Dec spread shed $1.00 to close at less than $2.00 backwardation.
"The gas oil was sold heavily into the close, but there was no real crack activity pushing it down," a broker said.
Traders focused on the record delivery into the expired Nov IPE contract, which produced barging delays in Rotterdam.
